headline: Humana Jumps 7% on Barclays Upgrade and $515 Target; UnitedHealth Nudges Higher
body:
A fresh analyst upgrade is sending Humana shares sharply higher, and the rally stands apart from a quiet managed care group. Humana stock is up 7% to $406.42 in the current session. That jump leaves Humana shares up 60% year to date, extending a powerful run that was well underway before the upgrade arrived.

Meanwhile, UnitedHealth Group stock is up 0.7% to $377.77, a far smaller gain than the one lifting Humana. Across the sector, the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund is essentially unmoved. At the same time, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust is up 0.5%, reflecting modest gains in the broad market.

The wide gap between Humana stock and its benchmarks keeps the story tightly focused on a single company and a single research call. Just one firm's change of heart is driving a daily move of this size, a sign of how sensitive Humana shares remain to shifts in analyst sentiment. Momentum like this can attract more buyers, although it can also reverse quickly when the news flow goes quiet.

Barclays Moves Humana to Overweight

Barclays upgraded Humana to Overweight from Neutral and raised its price target to $515 from $407. That combination reflects a change in an analyst's view, separate from any announcement by Humana itself, and moving from Neutral to Overweight takes Barclays off the sidelines on Humana stock, which marks a meaningful shift in conviction.

Humana Moves Apart From Managed Care

UnitedHealth Group stock is posting only a small advance, and that quiet response keeps the rally concentrated in Humana. A genuine sector reappraisal would usually lift the largest insurers together, and that pattern hasn't shown up alongside the Humana move. Humana stock, by contrast, is trading on a catalyst specific to the insurer.

Health care as a group is flat. The broad market is inching higher, so Humana stock is climbing with little help from its surroundings. That background matters, because sector tailwinds often buffer a stock when an upgrade-driven pop starts to cool, and without that support, Humana shares depend more heavily on whether the Barclays view gains wider acceptance.

For holders of Humana stock, the isolation cuts both ways. Company-specific rallies can hold up if other analysts come around to the same view, but such moves can also fade quickly if the upgrade stands alone and the sector stays flat.

Weighing the Bull and Bear Case for Humana

Optimists on Humana can point to the shift itself. Barclays abandoned a neutral stance and attached a new target, a combination that carries more weight than a routine revision. Momentum in Humana stock adds to that argument, since the shares entered the upgrade on a strong run.

However, the catch for Humana is that the move rests entirely on one analyst's review. Nothing new came from the company, and the business had already carried Humana stock a long way before Barclays weighed in. What Barclays now sees in the earnings path that it didn't see before is a question these figures leave uncertain.

Weighing both sides, Humana stock offers a clear case of sentiment moving ahead of fresh company information. That setup can reward patience if more analysts follow Barclays, and it can punish late buyers if the upgrade ends up standing alone.

What to Watch Next

Follow-through from other research firms could decide whether Humana stock holds its gain. Traders should look for fresh rating changes on Humana stock, since a second upgrade could extend the case beyond a single firm. Any cautious note from elsewhere could quickly test the strength of the move.

With Humana stock having already run this far, a moderate approach to sizing makes sense. Investors building their Humana exposure should keep their positions modest and add in stages. A sharp run can leave their existing holding larger than intended, so a periodic review of their allocation belongs in the plan.

Humana's upcoming quarterly earnings report is the next scheduled test of the Barclays call. Humana stock is worth monitoring for signs that the rally is holding up ahead of that release. Until other firms weigh in, the Barclays upgrade remains the main pillar under the latest leg higher.

headline: Meta Stock Surges 11% on AI Monetization Hopes
body:
As tech giants have continued to pour billions of dollars into the current artificial intelligence (AI) landscape, skepticism has grown over when those massive investments will start paying dividends — or whether there will be any dividends at all. Today, however, the market narrative is shifting as companies start demonstrating viable revenue streams from AI. Meta Platforms (META) is one such company that has unveiled plans for AI-related revenue.

Meta Platforms is a global tech and social media powerhouse operating platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Threads, and more under its "Family of Apps." Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, Meta has also started to aggressively pivot toward the use of artificial intelligence, custom silicon, and consumer AI products like Muse and Meta AI. Let's take a closer look.

META stock has staged a dramatic comeback after experiencing some turbulence in the market in 2026. On Sept. 21, the stock shot higher by more than 11%, then set a new 52-week high of $779.82 on Sept. 24 after months of underperformance.

Shares of META were falling on a year-to-date (YTD) basis earlier this year, weighed down by soaring AI investments and disappointing second-quarter figures. However, the launch of Muse AI has helped ignite a powerful rally in the stock, with shares now up 14% YTD.

By comparison, the S&P 500 Communications Services Sector ($SRTS) — which includes major telecom and media names — has posted modest gains for much of the year. Meta's recent spike and AI-driven rally have helped the stock outperform even its own sector, underscoring investment sentiment.

Meta Platforms reported its second-quarter 2026 results on July 29. The company showed revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year (YOY) and edging past the $60.2 billion analyst consensus estimate. However, diluted EPS came in at $6.18, missing the $7.22 estimate by more than 14% and snapping a streak of earnings beats as surging AI-related costs overwhelmed strong top-line growth.

Total costs and expenses surged 55% YOY to $42.03 billion, including $2.4 billion in legal charges and $1.18 billion in severance tied to an 8,000-employee headcount reduction, compressing Meta's GAAP operating margin to 31% from 43% a year earlier. Management guided Q3 revenue to $61 billion to $64 billion, while Wall Street estimates revenue of about $63 billion for the quarter. The company also narrowed its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $130 billion to $145 billion. CEO Mark Zuckerberg said that "AI is accelerating our core business today and opening the door to entirely new enterprise opportunities," while executives highlighted early traction from Meta's new enterprise AI cloud offering and the viral consumer adoption of Muse as key emerging monetization pathways.

Shares of Meta Platforms spiked more than 11% on Monday following investor enthusiasm surrounding the company's AI monetization strategy. The rally outpaced the broader tech space even as the S&P 500 Communications Services Sector popped nearly 4%, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained close to 3%, and rival firms like Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL), Reddit (RDDT), Netflix (NFLX), and Pinterest (PINS) made similar small gains.

Meta's recent spike continued its rally from early September, when it jumped following the initial Muse AI rollout and its acquisition of Swedish startup Stilla.ai.

Analysts have increasingly linked these catalysts to Meta's potential to unlock revenue streams beyond traditional digital advertising, including subscriptions, transactions, and business messaging monetization across WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram. That's reinforcing growing confidence that Meta's massive AI investments are beginning to translate into tangible, diversified growth.

Meta Platforms' explosive rally around Muse and broader AI monetization prospects has reignited investor confidence that the company's massive AI investments are finally translating into diversified revenue streams beyond advertising.

Wall Street remains overwhelmingly bullish. Overall, META stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating from 54 analysts with coverage. headline: Meta misled users about Facebook data practices, New Mexico jury finds
body:
A jury in Santa Fe, New Mexico, found on Friday that Meta Platforms misled the state's residents in a case arising from allegations that a political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent.

The verdict followed a two-week trial over a lawsuit filed by New Mexico's attorney general in 2021, three years after news reports revealed that the firm, Cambridge Analytica, had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

A Meta spokesperson said the company disagreed with the verdict and would continue to defend itself "against efforts to distort our record."

"Meta's platforms are forums for free expression," the spokesperson said. "We have a First Amendment right to manage those platforms in a way we believe best serves the interests of our community. This means prioritizing free speech, protecting our users' information and giving them control over their data."

At a press conference after the verdict was announced, New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said the case revealed "in stark detail the way in which this company plays fast and loose with the rules."

The state accused Meta of misleading New Mexicans about how it shared user data with third parties and enforced policies on hate speech and misinformation. New Mexico argued that Facebook failed to disclose that it sold user data to outside parties and allowed harmful content to spread when doing so benefited the company's bottom line.

Jurors found 26 of 29 statements identified by the state were misleading, including comments about user data, hate speech and misinformation. They rejected claims that Meta misled consumers in statements about its efforts to remove harmful content and its fact-checking practices.

Judge Francis Mathew will now determine civil penalties after jurors found more than 43 million violations, based on the number of people affected by the company's misleading statements. Under New Mexico law, Mathew can award up to $5,000 per violation.

Torrez said his office is evaluating how much to seek but will push for the maximum penalty based on the jury's findings.

The state will also ask Mathew to direct Meta to make changes, which could include corrections to its past misstatements as well as an audit of the way it manages user data, Torrez said.

The state's lawsuit focused on specific statements, including comments made by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg or in company blog posts, that New Mexico said made people believe they had control over the personal information they shared on the site, or that the site had blanket policies for how it dealt with hate speech or misinformation. Meta was selling the data to third-party apps, like the one that Cambridge Analytica relied on, and had exceptions to its policies for certain users, the state said.

Attorneys for Meta had argued at trial that the allegedly misleading statements were cherry-picked snippets that ignored critical context from the same statements, in which the company had repeatedly acknowledged its handling of misinformation or privacy issues was not perfect.

Meta also denied that it sells users' information.

Reuters viewed the trial on Courtroom View Network.

The verdict marks the second time in six months a jury in Santa Fe has weighed a lawsuit brought by the state of New Mexico against Meta Platforms.

In the first trial, which ended in March, a Santa Fe jury found Meta misled users about young users' safety on its Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp platforms and ordered the company to pay $375 million in civil penalties. After a second phase of that trial, a judge directed the company to pay $567 million into a New Mexico fund for teen mental health and ordered Meta to implement measures to protect teen Facebook and Instagram users in New Mexico.

A few weeks after the judge's ruling, Meta reached a sweeping settlement with 47 US states, Washington, D.C., and US territories, agreeing to pay a maximum of about $16.7 billion to resolve claims that it designed Facebook and Instagram to addict young children. As part of that deal, it agreed to pay a handful of states that had sued the company over privacy violations related to Cambridge Analytica $459 million to resolve those cases.

New Mexico was not part of the settlement, so its case over Cambridge Analytica moved forward to trial.

headline: Qualcomm (QCOM) Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
body:
Shares of wireless chipmaker Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) jumped 5.7% in the afternoon session after the stock rebounded from the previous session as the company announced the renewal of its global patent license agreement with Apple.

According to a press release published by Qualcomm, the renewed agreement will officially take effect on April 1, 2027, allowing the iPhone maker to continue utilizing the chipmaker's patented wireless technologies in exchange for ongoing royalty payments.

Because Apple represents a massive portion of the global smartphone market, securing this long-term extension provides crucial stability and removes a significant source of uncertainty for the chipmaker. Investors have actively bid up the stock over the past two sessions, treating the announcement as a major de-risking event that provides clear, long-term visibility into Qualcomm's high-margin future licensing revenue.

Ultimately, this continuation rally reflects Wall Street's relief that "Qualcomm has locked down its most important licensing partnership well into the next decade, guaranteeing a reliable cash flow stream even if broader hardware upgrade cycles experience near-term fluctuations."

Qualcomm's shares are very volatile and have had 28 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move occurred 4 days ago when the stock gained 7.4% on news that positive bilateral talks between the U.S. and China eased trade tensions, while retreating crude oil prices and falling Treasury yields revitalized market risk appetite. The semiconductor sector remains uniquely vulnerable to geopolitical developments and macroeconomic pressures due to its interconnected global supply chains and substantial capital requirements. Signs of constructive dialogue ahead of an upcoming U.S.-China summit help mitigate investor concerns over potential export controls and international trade barriers affecting key hardware producers.

At the same time, falling oil prices relieve broader inflationary headwinds, and declining Treasury yields provide support for equity valuations in high-growth technology industries. These converging macro factors triggered a broad rally across major artificial intelligence chipmakers, underscoring how macroeconomic stability and international diplomacy directly drive industry sentiment.

Qualcomm is up 18.7% since the beginning of the year, but at $205.33 per share, it is still trading 18.2% below its 52-week high of $251.02 from May 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Qualcomm's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,538.

headline: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
body:
The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to appear at an Australian Senate inquiry on AI, the head of the probe said on Sunday, days after the revelation that a rogue OpenAI bot had hacked the country's health-system database.

The Medicare breach, condemned by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US.

OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital Canberra on Thursday, said a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party, who chairs the probe.

OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

The OpenAI agent's incursion on one of the country's most used government agencies may prompt Albanese's Labor government to toughen AI-specific laws it is readying for next year, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra's ban on social media for teens, tech policy experts say.

The Senate inquiry is examining the potential impacts of AI and data centres on Australian communities, industries, water and energy. It is one of several state and federal probes into AI.

"There are serious questions for Sam Altman to answer about the OpenAI hack of Australian government websites," Hanson-Young said in a statement. Altman and Amodei "must front up, face the Senate's questions and have an honest conversation about what effective, lasting regulation of this industry should look like", she said.

Albanese, who revealed the June breach of Medicare on Thursday, called it "unacceptable", saying he had voiced "extreme concern" to Altman.

OpenAI says it only learned of the breach — one of at least four of Australian government websites — in August. It says the incident was not intentional and did not compromise any private information.

headline: Boeing Drops 3% as 737 MAX Landing Software Glitch Draws Regulator Review; GE Aerospace Eases, RTX Treads Water
body:
A newly reported software defect on the 737 MAX is pulling Boeing lower, and the pressure is landing almost entirely on one name. Boeing stock is down 3% to $192.98, extending a slide that has left the shares down 11% year to date.

Shares of GE Aerospace, which builds the LEAP engines that power the MAX, are down 0.7% to $324.74, a slight dip next to Boeing's loss. Meanwhile, shares of RTX are up 0.2% to $189.81, essentially treading water. Defense contractor Lockheed Martin Corp. carries minimal exposure to the MAX and sits on the fringe of the story.

Fund-level readings show only modest pressure. Across the sector, the iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF is down 0.5%. At the same time, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust is down 0.28%, leaving Boeing's decline well apart from both the sector fund and the broad market.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Boeing identified a software glitch on the MAX narrowbody that can disable an automated navigation function during a landing following a missed approach. According to the report, the bug emerged after a cockpit software update and can occur when pilots alter their planned flight path after that aborted approach, and in some circumstances the Boeing issue leaves pilots flying manually without some autopilot functions at low altitude.

Boeing notified airlines of the problem in late August, and the issue has since drawn concern among industry officials and a review by U.S. regulators. That review's outcome is the central unresolved question for the company, because the scope of any required fix could determine how long the pressure on Boeing stock lasts.

The bear case for Boeing starts with timing. Airlines learned of the defect from Boeing. That was weeks before the Journal's report carried it to the broader market, and the gap lands while the company's leadership is working to show progress on stability, safety, quality, and on-time performance. Fresh regulatory scrutiny of the MAX cuts directly against that operational-progress narrative for Boeing.

Labor adds another layer of uncertainty for Boeing. A ratification vote is open for the union. The union represents the company's Puget Sound engineering and technical employees, and the vote covers a tentative four-year contract that Reuters reported the two sides reached after members rejected an earlier offer. Complicating matters, the current contract expires in early October, and Boeing's chief executive stated in September that the MAX production ramp is taking longer than planned.

Boeing stock trades below its 50-day moving average of $214.37 while holding above its 52-week low of $176.77. That positioning suggests Boeing stock was already under strain before the bug showed up, which may leave the company little room to absorb another setback.

Boeing's bull case rests on the nature of the defect. Cockpit software is where the flaw lives, which, in this reading, points to a code update as the likely remedy and keeps the problem away from Boeing's airframes and factory floors. Such a framing gives the company a narrower problem to solve than a structural or production defect would.

Boeing is targeting certification of the 737-7 and 737-10 in 2026, with first deliveries expected in 2027. A software patch alone may leave that schedule intact, and the company's record backlog of $715 billion, including more than 6,200 commercial aircraft, gives Boeing a deep order book to work through.

Everything turns on the U.S. regulatory review for Boeing. If regulators accept a software update as the remedy, the bug could fade into a contained episode for the company, but any requirement beyond that update could test the company's delivery timeline and the credibility of its recovery.

Boeing is carrying this loss on its own, with GE Aerospace stock down only slightly and RTX stock close to unchanged. That split marks the selloff as company-specific, which may keep the damage contained to Boeing as long as the review stays narrow.

Investors considering Boeing should keep their position sizes modest until U.S. regulators clarify what the fix requires. Scaling in gradually could help investors limit their risk if the review expands into broader remedies.

Any regulatory requirement beyond a software update is worth watching, since that outcome could decide which reading of Boeing holds. Separately, the union's ratification result and the contract expiration give the company additional near-term markers to track.

headline: Теѕlа Faces Q3 Delivery Test — JPMorgan Cuts Forecast, Flags Weakness In Two Key Markets
body:
Ahead of Теѕlа's closely watched third-quarter deliveries later this week, J.P. Morgan lowered its price target and slashed its delivery forecast, citing weaker-than-expected performance across its two largest markets.

ТЅLА shares edged 0.5% lower in pre-market trading Monday.

JPMorgan cut Теѕlа's price target to $415 from $445 while maintaining a 'Neutral' rating, according to TheFly. The firm said it expects Теѕlа to deliver about 482,000 vehicles in the third quarter (Q3), about 6.5% lower than its previous estimate of 516,000, citing weaker-than-expected deliveries in the U.S. and China.

Based on July and August data, the brokerage said Теѕlа's sales trends remained mixed across major markets. In August, Теѕlа's new vehicle registrations dipped nearly 13% in China and around 4% in the U.S.

JPMorgan's forecast adds to a wide range of expectations on Wall Street ahead of Теѕlа's Q3 numbers.

Goldman Sachs recently slashed its forecast to 435,000 vehicles from 490,000, saying weaker sales in the U.S., China and Europe could offset strength in export markets such as Southeast Asia, South America and Australia.

Barclays is more optimistic, forecasting 475,000 deliveries, while StoneX expects about 446,500. Теѕlа delivered 480,126 vehicles in Q2.

Overall, Теѕlа's European business has shown signs of improvement. EU registrations jumped nearly 53% in August, although Chinese rivals BYD, Chery and Leapmotor grew much faster. Across the broader EU, EFTA and the U.K. region, Теѕlа registrations rose just 4%.

JPMorgan also lowered its gross margin estimates, citing higher raw material costs, incentives offered during the quarter, and elevated interest rates.

Meanwhile, analysts continue to look beyond vehicle sales toward Теѕlа's AI, autonomous driving, energy storage, and robotics businesses. Barclays recently said Теѕlа's fundamentals have become "mostly an afterthought" relative to its broader AI story, while StoneX expects its fast-growing energy storage business to offset some of the losses in vehicle registrations.

Retail sentiment surrounding ТЅLА on Stocktwits has remained 'neutral' over the past 24 hours.

The shares are down 15% so far this year, the only stock among the so-called Magnificent 7 to trade in the red.

headline: Blackstone's $450 Billion Private Equity Business Loses Its Longtime Chief
body:
Blackstone's longtime head of private equity is set to leave the firm at year-end.

Joe Baratta is leaving the firm after 28 years leading the asset manager's private equity business, Bloomberg reported. Last year, Baratta was placed into a new role overseeing strategies within the private equity unit.

Blackstone manages approximately $450 billion in assets.

Baratta's role will not be filled, Bloomberg noted, citing an internal memo sent to employees last week. His departure leaves Blackstone with just two executives on its board: CEO Steve Schwarzman and President Jon Gray.

"Joe has spent years empowering a team of experienced investors to oversee our individual private equity strategies and funds. Given the strength of the leaders for each of our dedicated PE verticals today, we do not intend to replace Joe's role," Schwarzman and Gray wrote in the memo.

Baratta joined Blackstone in 1998 and later moved to London to help build out the firm's European private equity business, eventually becoming global head of strategy in 2012. During his tenure, he helped lead investments including Merlin Entertainments and Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc., both of which generated significant returns.

During Baratta's time at the firm, Blackstone expanded into a diversified alternative asset manager. Altogether, it oversees approximately $1.3 trillion in assets spanning private equity, real estate, infrastructure, credit and hedge funds.

Last year, Blackstone shifted Baratta into a broader private equity role. In his expanded role, Baratta helped develop the firm's AI investment strategy. He also secured golfer Tommy Fleetwood as the firm's first brand ambassador.

Baratta is reportedly interested in pursuing a career in politics.

The move comes after several high-profile leadership changes at the firm this year, with real estate chief Nadeem Meghji and growth strategy head Jon Korngold also stepping down.

In April, Blackstone launched a new division focused on alternative investments in AI and high-growth tech, including companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Jasvinder Khaira joined to lead that team, succeeding Korngold.

headline: Te​sla Pushes Roadster Event To Oct. 15 After Storm Forecast, Says It 'Can Only Be Held Outdoors'
body:
Te​sla on Monday pushed back the unveiling of its second-generation Roadster from Oct. 1 to Oct. 15, citing "severe conditions predicted" and saying the gathering "can only be held outdoors."

In a post on X, the company said it had been tracking forecasts with local meteorologists and would share more details later.

Te​sla had previously said the event would take place in the Waco area of central Texas, near SpaceX's McGregor test site. The company did not name a new venue yet.

TS​LA stock closed down 4% on Monday.

The Oct. 1 reveal had been confirmed only in mid-September, after Te​sla posted a "Go for launch" teaser and Elon Musk replied that the new Roadster would be unveiled on Oct. 1.

That itself was the latest in a long chain of missed targets. The prototype first appeared as a surprise at the Te​sla Semi event in November 2017, with production promised for 2020. The timeline later moved through 2022, 2023, 2024, and into 2025–26. In late 2025, Musk floated an April 1, 2026 demo, then late spring, then August. Production is now discussed for 2027 or 2028.

The upcoming Roadster is a tribute to Te​sla's first car, the 2008 Roadster sports car, which kickstarted the company's EV business.

The original 2017 pitch was a four-seat electric sports car with a claimed 1.9-second 0–60 mph time, more than 620 miles of range, and a top speed above 250 mph. Musk later raised the stakes with a SpaceX-derived cold-gas thruster package that he has said could cut that time toward, and even under, one second and briefly lift the car off the ground.

Reservation holders who put down deposits as early as 2017 will now wait another fortnight.

Musk has previously dismissed the financial impact of the Roadster, calling it a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially." Rather than being a core revenue driver for Te​sla, Musk famously noted that the ultra-luxury sports car is "not even the icing on the cake, but the cherry on the icing on the cake."

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TS​LA stock stayed 'neutral' over the past 24 hours, while message volume remained 'low.'

TS​LA stock has fallen 21% year-to-date.
